messages:
leah: FYI we just received an escalation from a customer (FinaFlow) — they report p95 ~250ms but p99 jumped to ~1.6s on the /v1/generate route after last night's runtime push. They attached a short repro and said it started ~02:10 UTC. :rotating_light:

maria: thanks, leah. do we have customer route/model id and exact timestamps? any sample payloads?

leah: pasted from their ticket: model: open-llm/tiny-qa-v1, route: /v1/generate, request window 02:09:40-02:15:10 UTC. attaching their minimal payload: 

```json
{"prompt":"Summarize the following:\n...","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.0}
```

leah: also they included the Console latency graph: p50~180ms p95~240ms p99~1600ms. They say no error spikes, just tail latency.

sam: I pulled internal traces — there are long kernel execution bursts for step 1 of decode. We switched a kernel selector tweak in the rollout: enable_flashattn=true + sdpa_autotune=fast in commit a7b2c3 (deployed 02:05 UTC).

maria: that's the suspect. a7b2c3 flips the kernel priority to prefer FlashAttention-v2 kernels over SDPA in many cases. The change improved median in validation but we saw variance on some sequence-length distributions.

jon: can we reproduce against their payload? I spun up a small runner and sent 200 concurrent requests like their pattern. p99 surfaces after about 50 concurrent sessions — looks like certain seq_len combinations choose a fallback SDPA path with suboptimal scheduling.

maria: interesting — the scheduler we merged defers to "compat_fallback" kernel when the tuned flash kernel reports a workspace_alloc failure at runtime. But the failure rate is tiny; when the fallback hits it spawns a different kernel that blocks the SMs longer. That could explain occasional long tails.

kerneld: dumping kernel selection logs for model open-llm/tiny-qa-v1 on the affected host: 

```
[02:06:12] kernel_select: flash_v2 preferred
[02:06:12] flash_v2: try_compile -> success
[02:06:13] flash_v2: launch -> runtime_alloc_failed (66% free) -> fallback to sdpa_legacy
[02:06:13] sdpa_legacy: launch -> queued -> 1.1s exec
[02:06:14] flash_v2: subsequent launch -> success
```

kerneld: so intermittent workspace_alloc failures during busy GC windows cause fallback to legacy SDPA which is much slower for this model on the current kernel binary.

sam: are the failures from real OOM or fragmented allocation? The logs show "runtime_alloc_failed" not OOM.

maria: looks like fragmentation / ephemeral allocation. The new flash kernel uses a larger temporary workspace and we didn't account for a hotpath where KV cache hits change the allocation pattern. Under the customer's traffic mix the allocator sometimes returns an allocation that violates the kernel's alignment constraints and it bails to fallback.

leah: customer asked for a quick mitigation — they need p99 back to ~300ms within the hour if possible.

maria: initial mitigations: 1) toggle sdpa_autotune back to "safe" to prefer SDPA versions that are less likely to hit fallback, 2) temporarily disable flash preference (enable_flashattn=false) on the route, 3) pin the customer to the older model runtime variant that used the previous compile flags. Any of those will help.

sam: I'll push a route-level override to disable flash preference for FinaFlow and similar customers. Going to do a canary on 1 host first. deploy-bot: initiating canary config rollout for route /v1/generate (override: enable_flashattn=false) commit=deconfig-20260315-1

deploy-bot: canary started on host r-12-az1 at 02:28 UTC

jon: while that's rolling we should also flip sdpa_autotune to "conservative" cluster-wide to reduce workspace size requests. I can do a hot-config change on the pool. Maria, can you assemble the precise flag set to revert?

maria: revert plan: 
- set enable_flashattn=false for canary routes
- sdpa_autotune=conservative cluster-wide (hot-config)
- recompile flash kernels with lower temp_workspace (next patch) and revert commit a7b2c3 if tests show improvement
- backfill allocator alignment sanity checks to avoid spurious fallback

maria: quick commands: 
```
# route override (canary)
redwood route update --route /v1/generate --customer FinaFlow --set enable_flashattn=false

# sdpa autotune hot-config
redwood config set cluster.sdpa_autotune conservative --apply
```

sam: applied the route override to FinaFlow canary host. monitoring now.

(02:34) deploy-bot: canary rollout success on host r-12-az1

jon: cluster sdpa_autotune -> conservative applied at 02:35 UTC.

(02:46) sam: preliminary metrics from the canary: p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 320ms for canary host. Medians unchanged. Looks promising.

leah: customer confirmed a quick improvement in their next few requests, they're seeing p99 ~330ms. :thumbsup:

maria: good. next steps: schedule a controlled cluster-wide rollback of the flash preference until we land the kernel compile fix and allocator checks. We'll run extended load tests with the customer's seq_len distribution to validate. I'll tag this as a Sev-2 until full root cause and fix are merged.

kerneld: quick note for RCA: record kernel runtime_alloc_failed counts, workspace size distribution, and KV cache hit patterns. I'll add those metrics to the per-route dashboard.

jon: ops tasks: 1) rollback route defaults for enable_flashattn across affected release (a7b2c3) 2) coordinate with infra to schedule compile job with reduced temp_workspace and alignment support 3) run 24h soak with FinaFlow-like workload.

sam: I'll keep the canary and measure for 30m before rolling wider. If p99 stays <400ms we can do a gradual rollout of the conservative autotune change and then the flash pref rollback.

leah: I updated the customer ticket with status & mitigation steps and ETA for full fix (48-72h). They asked for a postmortem once fixed.

maria: thanks all. action items assigned: 
- maria: open PR to reduce flash temp_workspace + add alignment checks (PR #4521)
- kerneld: add runtime_alloc_failed counter & dashboard panel
- jon: orchestrate controlled rollback and soak
- sam: monitor canary and coordinate progressive rollout
- leah: keep customer updated, collect any other example payloads

maria: tagging for follow-up: @eng-runtime @eng-sre @support. We'll reconvene in the incident channel if anything regresses.

(03:10) sam: canary stable for 40m, p99 ~310-350ms. marking resolved for now; keeping Sev-2 until kernels are fixed.

(06:05) maria: PR #4521 opened, CI perf tests running. I'll post results here when available.

(23:15) jon: reminder — don't flip flash preference back until PR validated. We'll publish RCA draft tomorrow.

leah: customer acknowledged and requested a short summary + timeline once RCA is ready.

---
Notes: repro pattern used for testing: run_locust with concurrency=60, request_payload as above, KV cache behavior randomized to 0/1 to simulate hits. Look for runtime_alloc_failed spikes in kernel logs.
